statements.status_notes:
Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA bcprov on all (core modules).
This vulnerability is associated with program files G3413CTRBlockCipher.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, from 1.82 before 1.84.
statements.impact_statement: This affected bcprov-jdk18on from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, and from 1.82 before 1.84. This repository now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85, past the fixed range, as defense-in-depth. Independent of version, the vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: a source review found zero references to G3413CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147, GOST, G3413, CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147Engine, or GOST28147ParameterSpec anywhere in this codebase, so the GOST 28147 CTR mode cipher classes required to reach this vulnerability are never invoked.

statements.status_notes: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.85, Lazy ASN.1 sequence forcing resets nesting-depth guard. This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java LTS before 2.73.12, and Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bc-fips 1.0.2.7 (1.0.X series), 2.0.2 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.3 (2.1.X series).
statements.impact_statement: This affected bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85. This repository now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85, past the fixed version, as defense-in-depth. Independent of version, a source review found zero direct `import org.bouncycastle.` usage anywhere in this codebase, and zero references to LazyEncodedSequence, ASN1StreamParser, ASN1InputStream, BERSequenceParser, DLSequenceParser, or LazyConstructionEnumeration. The only Bouncy Castle usage in production code is Snowflake private-key loading through a shaded `net.snowflake.client.jdbc.internal.org.bouncycastle.*` namespace — a different package entirely from the standalone bcprov-jdk18on artifact this CVE affects, and one that never touches the vulnerable ASN.1 parsing classes.

statements.status_notes:
Covert timing channel vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA core on all (core modules). This vulnerability is associated with program files FrodoEngine.Java.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.71 before 1.84.
statements.impact_statement: Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA FrodoEngine covert timing channel affects versions 1.71 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1318), but grep for FrodoEngine, Frodo, org.bouncycastle.pqc, pqc.crypto.frodo, and BCPQC across Java sources returned no matches, so the vulnerable Frodo post-quantum cryptography code path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.85, Name Constraints bypass via trailing dot in rfc822Name and URI. This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java LTS before 2.73.12, and Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bc-fips 1.0.2.7 (1.0.X series), 2.0.2 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.3 (2.1.X series).
statements.impact_statement: This affected bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85. This repository now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85, past the fixed version, as defense-in-depth. Independent of version, a source review found zero direct `import org.bouncycastle.` usage anywhere in this codebase, and zero references to NameConstraints, rfc822Name, GeneralSubtree, or PKIXNameConstraintValidator. The only Bouncy Castle usage in production code is Snowflake private-key loading through a shaded `net.snowflake.client.jdbc.internal.org.bouncycastle.*` namespace — a different package entirely from the standalone bcprov-jdk18on artifact this CVE affects, and one that never exercises certificate name-constraint validation.
